reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order list and the refund list so I can confirm the handoff matches the ledger.
Orders are listed, so next I'll pull the refund list to cross-check W2's handoff against the ledger before any payout.
The refund list matches W2's handoff exactly (orders 231, 234, 235), so the ledger is consistent. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 36083 matches its orders (18974 + 17109) with no refunds, so the ledger is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 10785 matches its orders (21055 + 11644 = 32699) minus refunds (17910 + 4004 = 21914), so the ledger is consistent. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 29267 matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus the refund on order 235 (1660). All three balances reconcile with the ledger, so there is no reason to hold. I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded and birch's net balance (10785) reconciled with the orders and refunds. Next I'll record birch's payout.
Cobalt's net balance is 29267, which matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus the refund on order 235 (1660). That reconciles, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully, and each amount matched the reconciled net balance: acme 36083, birch 10785, cobalt 29267. The batch is complete.
